text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on May 2 in history:
1519 - Leonardo da Vinci, Italian sculptor, scientist and painter of the "Mona Lisa" and the "Last Supper", died.
1660 - Pietro Alessandro Gaspare Scarlatti, Italian composer of operas and religious works, born.
1670 - The Hudson's Bay Company was chartered by the English crown and given a monopoly of the trade into Hudson Bay, Canada.
1729 - Catherine II or Catherine the Great, Empress of Russia, born. Noted for her willingness to participate with political and cultural developments in Europe.
1860 - The founder of modern Zionism, Theodor Herzl, born in Budapest.
1864 - Giacomo Meyerbeer, German Grand opera composer of "Les Huguenots" and "L'Africaine", died.
1885 - King Leopold II of Belgium was proclaimed king of the new Congo Free State.
1892 - Baron Manfred von Richthofen, German fighter ace, born; he shot down more than 80 enemy aircraft in World War One and became known as "The Red Baron".
1903 - Benjamin Spock, child care specialist and pediatrician, born in the United States.

1904 - Harry Lillis (Bing) Crosby, U.S. singer and actor, born. He became one of the most popular entertainers and his hit song "White Christmas" became the biggest selling single ever with worldwide sales exceeding 30 million copies.
1923 - Patrick Hillery, Irish politician, president from 1976-90, born. He negotiated Ireland's entry into the European Community in 1973 and was EC vice-president for three years
1933 - In Germany, Adolf Hitler banned trade unions.
1938 - King Moshoeshoe II of Lesotho born as Constantine Bereng Seeiso. A largely ceremonial king from 1960-90, he achieved some degree of power from 1986 following a military coup.
1945 - Berlin surrendered to the 1st White Russian and 1st Ukrainian armies; hostilities in Italy ceased as the surrender terms took effect; Hamburg opened negotiations for the surrender of the city.
1952 - The first scheduled jet airliner passenger service began with a BOAC Comet which flew from London to Johannesburg carrying 36 passengers.
1953 - In Jordan, King Hussein formally acceeded to the throne after his father King Talal, was deposed. In Iraq, King Feisal II assumed power.
1957 - Senator Joe McCarthy, U.S. politician and Republican senator famous for his anti-communist witch-hunts, died.
1964 - Lady Nancy Astor, who became the first woman MP to sit in the British House of Commons in 1919, died.
1965 - The first communications satellite for relaying television pictures went into operation; the "Early Bird" transmitted to 24 countries.
1969 - The British passenger liner Queen Elizabeth 2, left on her maiden voyage to New York.
1972 - John Edgar Hoover, founder and director of the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation since 1924, died in Washington.
1982 - In the Falklands war, the Argentine cruiser General Belgrano was sunk by the British submarine Conqueror; over 350 men were killed.
1992 - The Yugoslav Army seized Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic after fierce fighting in Sarajevo.
1994 - President F.W. de Klerk conceded victory to Nelson Mandela in the country's historic all-race elections.
1995 - Serb missiles exploded in the heart of Zagreb, killing six people.
